clue.text: How the dealer struggles to be sincere

indicators.note: struggles suggests letters thrashing about, so the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a card dealer or trader manages to come across as genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggles' rearranges all twelve letters of HOW THE DEALER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe feeling given fully and genuinely, with nothing held back.

clue.text: Argument about son in love

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for an argument is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
in, meaning fashionable, is hip

explanation.surface: A quarrel concerning a son who has fallen for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ROW into WOR; 'in' is not a link word but HIP, as in trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone deeply is to idolise them, so the verb love fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Spare bishop from inconvenience

indicators.note: bishop from inconvenience means the bishop's letter is taken away from that word

parts.note: bother is trouble or inconvenience
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A plea to save a bishop from some nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' reads as a verb (let off), but it is the adjective: the extra one.
explanation.definitionFit: An additional or alternative item, as in the remaining one in reserve, is a spare.

clue.text: Try to stop each victory of US

parts.note: to stop is to end
of us is ours, the possessive our

explanation.surface: An attempt to halt every American triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of US' is not the United States but the pronoun: belonging to us gives OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as nouns or verbs: an effort or attempt to achieve something.

clue.text: Reportedly, Cockney bloke spotted Jacob's brother

indicators.note: Reportedly says the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H, so 'he saw' comes out as 'e saw

explanation.surface: A Londoner apparently caught sight of a Biblical figure's sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class East London accent, which drops initial H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the hairy elder twin who sold his birthright to Jacob is his brother.

clue.text: Some Tories linger for alcoholic drink

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few Conservatives hang around waiting for booze.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'for', which is only a link word joining the wordplay to 'alcoholic drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: A white wine made from the grape of that name, chiefly German, is an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Welcome cuts and so forth, in principle

indicators.note: the greeting cuts into, so it sits inside, the abbreviation for and so forth

parts.note: etc. is short for et cetera, and so forth
hi is a word of greeting or welcome

explanation.surface: In theory, people welcome spending cuts and similar measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welcome cuts' reads as approving of austerity; 'cuts' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral rule or standard of conduct is an ethic, close in sense to a guiding principle.

clue.text: Resurrect memories of Unionists admitting terrible greed

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the party abbreviation contains the other letters

parts.note: DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of the following word are mangled

explanation.surface: Northern Irish politicians recall awful avarice.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party; 'terrible' scrambles the greed and 'admitting' sets it inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to bring an old, often unwelcome matter back to attention, as if hauling it from a riverbed.

clue.text: Keen to include good, uplifting music

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
to include means the word for keen holds the letter inside

parts.note: eager means keen

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for upbeat, cheerful tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts G in EAGER to make EAGGER, which 'uplifting' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jamaican popular style with an offbeat rhythm is an example of music.

clue.text: Dryer heat possibly requires one to do this

definitions.text: Dryer heat possibly requires one to do this

indicators.note: possibly hints that the preceding letters might form another arrangement

explanation.surface: Hot, dry conditions mean you must drink more water.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: drier heat makes one need to restore fluids, while 'possibly' rearranges DRYER HEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore lost water to the body is what hot dry weather demands of people.

clue.text: Nag Republican wearing tights

indicators.note: wearing means the letter is dressed in the garment, so it goes inside

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights

explanation.surface: Pester an American politician dressed in tights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a verb (pester) but is the noun: an old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nag is an informal word for an old or poor-quality steed.

clue.text: Cheer hot tennis player with shaved head

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: shaved head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: Andy Murray is the Scottish tennis champion

explanation.surface: Applaud a sizzling tennis star who has had his head shaved.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy Murray, a Scot, won Wimbledon twice; 'with shaved head' drops his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of joy or approval shouted out is a cheer.

clue.text: Depression of jet-setter?

parts.note: jet is a deep black colour
a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: The low mood of a wealthy international traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet-setter' splits into 'jet' (black) and 'setter' (a gun dog). The phrase is Churchill's well-known name for his depression.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for melancholy or clinical low mood, famously used by Winston Churchill.

clue.text: Silicon filtered out of rank medicinal drink

indicators.note: filtered out of means the element's symbol is removed from the word for rank

parts.note: a position is a rank or status
Si is the chemical symbol for silicon

explanation.surface: An element strained out of a foul-smelling remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like an adjective (smelly) describing the drink, but it is a noun: one's standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid dose of medicine, or a magic brew, is a potion.

clue.text: Theory oddly lacking conclusion

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and fifth letters of the word

parts.note: minus means without or lacking

explanation.surface: A strange theory with no proper ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the odd letters of THEORY, giving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stop or end point of a route is its end, a conclusion.

clue.text: Introduction to "Happy New Year" composed in unspecified place

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so these letters are rearranged
the introduction to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A New Year greeting written somewhere or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges H (from 'Introduction to Happy') with NEWYEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at any location whatever, with no particular spot named.

clue.text: Contemptuous and essentially conceited group of criminals

parts.note: with can mean and, as in 'bread with butter'

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence or centre, so the central letter is taken

parts.note: a ring is a gang, as in a smuggling ring

explanation.surface: Someone scornful, vain at heart, belonging to a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is not a link word but WITH; 'essentially' takes the middle E of CONCEITED.
explanation.definitionFit: A scathing look or remark is scornful, full of disdain.

clue.text: Someone who desecrates instrument on hill

parts.note: a viola is a stringed instrument
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A vandal playing a string instrument on a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a rocky peak, found on the moors of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: One who profanes or breaks a sacred place or rule is a transgressor of it.

clue.text: Picture left by scoundrel touring Italy

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the rogue's word surrounds the country letter

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A painting abandoned by a villain on a trip around Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts I inside RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted or photographed likeness of a person is a type of picture.

clue.text: Robbery plot with no disadvantages

indicators.note: with no means the word for drawbacks is removed

parts.note: a conspiracy is a plot
cons, as in pros and cons, are disadvantages

explanation.surface: A theft scheme with no downside.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft at sea, or the unauthorised copying of works, is a kind of robbery.

clue.text: Rejected help at supermarket bagging essential food item

indicators.note: Rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
bagging means the clue words hold the letters inside them, as a bag does

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone turned down assistance at the shop packing their groceries.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'bagging' into the definition, but it is the hiding signal: 'help at supermarket' bags ELPATS.
explanation.definitionFit: A basic foodstuff such as bread or rice that forms a main part of a diet.

clue.text: Pays out most of cost to protect Duke

indicators.note: to protect means wrapping round, so the shortened word holds the title letter
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: expense is cost

explanation.surface: A nobleman's bodyguard bill is mostly covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims EXPENSE to EXPENS; 'to protect' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money or use up resources is to disburse them, a synonym.

clue.text: Weather provided by sun god in autumn

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Climate brought by an ancient deity in the autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation, measured as an amount of rain, is an example of weather.

clue.text: Shambles as Rooney originally included in side

indicators.note: included in means one letter goes inside the word for side

parts.note: a face is a side, as of a cube or cliff

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A footballing fiasco when Wayne Rooney is picked for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' suggests a football team, but it is a face; Wayne Rooney was an England striker.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridiculous, chaotic mess of an event is a shambles.

clue.text: Parody beginning of show, and finish

indicators.note: beginning of means only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: to finish somewhere is to end up there

explanation.surface: A comedy sketch, from the opening of a show to the close.
explanation.definitionFit: A mocking imitation that sends something up is a parody.

clue.text: See fit Scandinavian in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means as spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a Dane is a Scandinavian from Denmark

explanation.surface: Choose to talk with someone from Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend to do something, as if granting a favour, is to see fit to do it.

clue.text: Dropping trousers, rector showing member

indicators.note: trousers as a verb means pockets, so the word for dung holds the letter

parts.note: a pat is a dropping, as in a cowpat

explanation.surface: A clergyman taking his trousers down and exposing himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' and 'trousers' change jobs: the dropping is a cowpat, and 'trousers' is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: A component or constituent piece of a whole is a member of it.

clue.text: The noise from cricket starts to cause havoc up Radcliffe Road

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of each following word are taken

explanation.surface: Crowd noise at a cricket match causes chaos in a Nottingham street.
explanation.walkthrough: Radcliffe Road is an end of Trent Bridge cricket ground, but the cricket is the chirping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The low trilling call of a cricket, nightjar or similar creature.

clue.text: Custom from Turkey: one daughter gets wasted in annexe

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

indicators.note: gets wasted means one letter is lost from the word

parts.note: an addition is an extension or annexe to a building
D is the abbreviation for daughter; one says only one of the two goes

explanation.surface: A Turkish practice where a girl gets drunk in an outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets wasted' takes one of the two Ds from ADDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-established practice handed down the generations is a custom.

clue.text: Spies soprano centre stage, wandering around

indicators.note: wandering around suggests the letters drift into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer moves about in the middle of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering around' rearranges only CENTRE STAGE; the soprano's S stays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Undercover operatives working for a government are spies.
